content.text:
This is a valid UX gap, not user error. [Discussion #13143](https://github.com/jdx/mise/discussions/13143) remains unanswered with no replies.

Current behavior:

- `mise bootstrap dotfiles status` reports only the path and conflict type; it discards the stored local/base/remote object details when formatting status ([apply.rs](/Users/jdx/.codex/worktrees/99ac/mise/src/system/history/sync/apply.rs:902)).
- The documented “Inspect the reported files” instruction is therefore misleading ([history.md](/Users/jdx/.codex/worktrees/99ac/mise/docs/history.md:288)).
- `mise bootstrap dotfiles history diff` compares checkpoints or the live tree, but cannot address the fetched remote conflict state ([diff.rs](/Users/jdx/.codex/worktrees/99ac/mise/src/cli/dotfiles/history/diff.rs:7)).
- Git mergetool cannot currently be used directly because mise’s repository is bare and never creates an unmerged Git index. The conflict is represented in mise’s `sync.json`, not as index stages.
- The reconciliation layer does retain base/local/remote objects, so native support is practical ([reconcile.rs](/Users/jdx/.codex/worktrees/99ac/mise/src/system/history/sync/reconcile.rs:111)).

For this specific unencrypted `config.toml` conflict, the present workaround is:

```sh
state_dir="${MISE_STATE_DIR:-${XDG_STATE_HOME:-$HOME/.local/state}/mise}"
repo="$state_dir/history/repo.git"

git --git-dir="$repo" diff \
  refs/heads/main refs/remotes/origin/setup \
  -- config/config.toml
```

A configured difftool should also work:

```sh
git --git-dir="$repo" difftool \
  refs/heads/main refs/remotes/origin/setup \
  -- config/config.toml
```

To preserve changes from both sides, edit the live file into the desired merged form, then:

```sh
mise bootstrap dotfiles save
mise bootstrap dotfiles pull --keep-local ~/.config/mise/config.toml
```

I would treat this as a small feature/bug fix: add a supported conflict-diff command that uses the exact stored conflict objects, handles decryption safely, and update status to point to it. Configured `difftool` support is straightforward; full `mergetool` support needs a temporary three-stage index plus careful handling of decrypted temporary files.

No repository changes or GitHub replies were made. The historical checkpoint search found the original sync work, but its session had no retained checkpoint explaining why conflict inspection was omitted.
